name: A year of a VAT-registered British trading company, filing quarterly on a year to 31 March

documents.why: A domestic purchase at the standard rate: box 7 takes the value and box 4 the input tax. The return has no box for the rate of a purchase, so this is the only place the 20 % shows.
A domestic sale at the standard rate: box 6 takes the value and box 1 the output tax.
The reduced rate: a second positive rate, which boxes 1 and 6 add to the standard one because the British return carries no breakdown by rate.

A zero-rated sale: box 6 and nothing in box 1. On the return it is indistinguishable from the exempt sale below, and in the ledger the two are different codes because only one of them carries a right to deduct.
Business entertainment: the Input Tax Order excludes the whole of the VAT from credit, so it lands on the account of the line it taxes and box 4 stays empty while box 7 still carries the value.
An exempt supply: the same two boxes as a zero-rated one, and the exemption reason code no published list carries.
An export of goods outside the United Kingdom: box 6 only. Since 2021 the word covers a supply to a member State of the Union too, which is the whole reason this pack carries no intra-Community tax.
An import of goods under postponed VAT accounting: one invoice fills boxes 1, 4 and 7 and nets to nothing in the ledger, which is the mechanism that replaced the intra-Community acquisition here.
The supplier's side of the construction reverse charge: box 6 carries the value and box 1 nothing, because the customer accounts for the tax.

A day of counter sales priced with the VAT already in it, which is how a British shop quotes to a consumer. The three lines are quoted gross — the third after 15 % off the marked price — and the engine takes the tax out of the group's gross, rounds it once as BR-CO-14 requires, and shares the base back over the lines: the invoice totals the 5 493.92 the customers actually paid, never a penny beside it. The three shares rounded on their own would come to a penny more than the base, so the last line carries the remainder, which is what makes this document worth keeping.

lines.name: Clearance rail, 15 % off the marked price

documents.why: The customer's side of the construction reverse charge: boxes 1, 4 and 7, and deliberately not box 6 — which is what distinguishes it from the service received below.

A service received from a supplier established outside the United Kingdom: the one amount the return prints in box 6 and in box 7 at once, which is why the pack defines it in a box of its own that both totals read.
A credit note on the standard-rated sale, in a later quarter than the invoice: every box the invoice filled, with the sign turned round, and no negative amount in the ledger.
The reduced rate on the buying side, in the last quarter of a year that does not run to 31 December: a British accounting reference date is the company's own.

payments.why: A payment that settles the standard-rated purchase exactly, VAT included.
A receipt that settles its invoice exactly and closes it.
A payment on account: it leaves an open item, which is what a real ledger holds and what a return computed from matchings has to survive.
